Docs/Replay/Guide

Replay

Old-host prop adoption

2 min readOdin × GodotPage source ↓
On this page ↓
CompatibilityEvidence and boundaries

Introduced in C8, this policy observes the authority's local player seat through Replay's recorded authority policy. World keeps the last known seat independently of lobby leadership. On a change from one player-host to another, a relic carried by the former host transfers to the successor and advances its version once. Other carriers and all avatars retain their identities. A dedicated successor has no avatar, so that transition releases the relic.

This follows Kit's host-takeover orphan sweep for non-avatar entities. This policy runs on the first committed simulation tick after restore. The checkpoint frame itself remains exact; gameplay and the Carry event are recorded together, can be audited/replayed, and roll back together on failure. Repeated observations of the same authority do not repeat the transfer. Version overflow aborts the tick.

The successor's ordinary player step attaches the adopted relic at (10, -12). Clients receive that state and effect through replication; they do not guess an authority change during prediction. The old host can return to its original avatar/seat. Its authority role and possession of the relic are distinct.

Compatibility#

Current content is 0x4341564552504c39, with authority policy revision 1. C8 adds authority_known and authority_seat to World. The old C3–C7 world descriptor is frozen in the converter; C1/C2 retain their earlier descriptors.

For C1–C7 imports, tools/upgrade_save preserves previous world/peer fields and seeds the new observation from the validated checkpoint header's local_seat. C8 imports already contain that observation and retain it unchanged. See the current conversion guide for accepted formats and the command. Conversion requires a new destination; it neither infers authority from the party leader nor edits the old file. A new host's first resumed tick applies adoption. Network protocol 7 and checkpoint envelope version 4 remain unchanged; the world schema and negotiated policy contract change explicitly.

Evidence and boundaries#

Pure tests check once-per-change adoption, other-carrier preservation, complete corrected-input state/events, dedicated successors and overflow rollback. Real native planned/crash takeovers check adoption in the first committed frame and continued movement/release. A three-browser planned takeover checks the same ownership transfer alongside the existing party/social recovery story. The four successor/guest carrier cases remain regression gates.

The policy covers relic possession after a player-host change. Original owner-streamed motion, disconnected-avatar floor gating, and broader visual/human comparisons require separate work. This policy is specific to Cavecrawl's non-avatar relic; other games choose their own response to the recorded observation.
